# The two flag games of ASSS 1.4.4, run UNMODIFIED: src/py/fg_turf.py (90 lines)
# and src/py/fg_wz.py (372 lines). There is no fg_wz.c or fg_turf.c anywhere in
# ASSS 1.4.4 -- both flag games are Python -- so these were produced by
# vectors/pyharness, which supplies the five interfaces they pick up at import
# time and executes their source as written. The only name injected into their
# namespace is `xrange`, because they are Python 2 source.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. The flagcore behind these modules is a plain store, not
# ASSS's flagcore.c, so these records are ground truth for the GAME modules --
# where flags spawn, how a drop is routed, when a win is declared -- and for
# nothing else. flagcore.c's own state machine is pinned separately, in
# vectors/flagcore.txt. The two files are meant to be read together.
#
#   # <label>    starts a scenario, with a fresh arena and a fresh module
#   settings <section>:<key>=<value>...   the arena config for that scenario
#   map flagcount=<n> solid=<n> noflags=<n>   the map the game sees: how many
#       turf flags, how many solid tiles and how many tiles inside a no-flag
#       region, each then listed one per line as 'solid <x> <y>' / 'noflag <x> <y>'
#   cbresult <callback> <value>   a scoring module's answer, scripted for this
#       scenario; CB_WARZONEWIN is the one that matters, since it decides the points
#   op FlagTouch <player> <fid> carried=<n>   how many flags that player already
#       holds, which is an input because fg_wz's carry limit tests it
#   op <call>    the entry point driven: attach, Init, FlagTouch, Cleanup, or
#       one of the module's own top-level functions, which in a live zone is
#       what its timers and callbacks call
#   current <n>  set fg_wz's live flag count directly, standing in for however
#       many flags its spawn timer had put out
#   place <fid> <state>/<carrier>/<x>/<y>/<freq>   put a flag straight into the
#       store, standing in for whatever flagcore would have done
#   log <line>   everything the module did during that step, in order: calls
#       into flagcore, PRNG draws and what they returned, callbacks it fired,
#       timers it set, and log lines it wrote
#   flags <n> <fid>:<state>/<carrier>/<x>/<y>/<freq>...   every reserved flag
#   arena <attr>=<value>...   the attributes the module hangs off the arena
#   sets <key>=<value>...     fg_wz's parsed [Flag] settings
#
# The PRNG is scripted: every draw a scenario needs is queued in advance and
# shown in the log, so nothing here depends on a seed.
#
# Rules these records pin:
#
# 1. fg_turf's Init sets CARRY_NONE, reserves one flag per turf flag on the map,
#    and puts every one of them FI_ONMAP at freq -1. Its FlagTouch sets the
#    state to FI_ONMAP again on every tag -- it never trusts what was there --
#    and fires CB_TURFTAG with the OLD freq read before the write and the new
#    freq taken from the player.
# 2. fg_wz parses Flag:FlagCount with a three-level try/except: '<min>-<max>'
#    first, then a bare integer for both, then 0 for both. So a malformed value
#    silently means no flags, and '5-' or '-5' falls all the way through to 0.
#    max is clipped to 0..255 and min to 0..max, in that order, so a min above
#    max is pulled DOWN to max rather than raising it.
# 3. The spawn timer only picks a new flag count when the current count is below
#    the minimum, and it picks it with prng.Number(min, max) -- so a zone whose
#    min and max differ gets a different number of flags each game.
# 4. spawn_flag tries up to 30 times, GROWING THE RADIUS BY ONE EACH TRY, and
#    rejects a spot that is already occupied by another flag on the map or that
#    lies in a region with a NOFLAGS chunk. Only after all 30 does it fall back
#    to the arena's centre, and the fallback is itself a spawn_flag call with
#    fallback disabled, so it can fail outright and log an error.
# 5. circular_random picks the radius and the angle as two separate uniform
#    draws, IN THAT ORDER, scales by the radius, offsets the centre by half a
#    tile, truncates toward zero with int(), and then wraps. The wrap is a
#    REFLECTION, not a clamp and not a modulo: a coordinate of -3 becomes 3 and
#    one of 1026 becomes 1020, looping until it lands in range.
# 6. A neuted flag is remembered in a list on the arena, and when the spawn
#    timer comes round it respawns AT THE POSITION IT WAS NEUTED AT, with the
#    freq it was neuted with, using DropRadius or SpawnRadius depending on
#    Flag:NeutCenter -- not at the arena's spawn point like a fresh flag.
# 7. Cleanup routes the ten reasons to three different behaviours: a plain drop,
#    a safe-zone drop and a team-kill drop all SPAWN the flag with their own
#    owned/centre settings, a team kill does nothing at all when
#    Flag:FriendlyTransfer is on, and ship change, freq change, leaving the
#    arena and 'other' NEUT the flag instead, which is a different function.
#    CLEANUP_KILL_NORMAL is in none of those branches, so fg_wz ignores it.
# 8. check_win counts flags in CONSECUTIVE RUNS of the same freq, resetting the
#    count whenever the freq changes, and a flag that is not on the map is
#    skipped WITHOUT resetting the run. A win needs every flag on the map, all
#    on one freq, and that freq not -1. The points come from the CB_WARZONEWIN
#    callback, with a hardcoded 1000 when nothing answers.
# 9. The loop right after it, the one the source comments '# just to check',
#    reads flag index `current` on every iteration instead of `i`. It is only an
#    assert, so it changes nothing, but a port that transcribes it faithfully
#    will be checking the wrong flag.
# turf: Init reserves one flag per turf flag, all unowned
map flagcount=5 solid=0 noflags=0
op attach
flags 0
op Init
log flagcore SetCarryMode 0
log flagcore ReserveFlags 5
log flagcore SetFlags 0 onmap/-/0/0/-1
log flagcore SetFlags 1 onmap/-/0/0/-1
log flagcore SetFlags 2 onmap/-/0/0/-1
log flagcore SetFlags 3 onmap/-/0/0/-1
log flagcore SetFlags 4 onmap/-/0/0/-1
flags 5 0:onmap/-/0/0/-1 1:onmap/-/0/0/-1 2:onmap/-/0/0/-1 3:onmap/-/0/0/-1 4:onmap/-/0/0/-1
arena fg_turf_fc=5 fg_turf_persist=1
op FlagTouch p0 0 carried=0
log flagcore SetFlags 0 onmap/-/0/0/0
log callback turftag (flags, p0, 0, -1, 0)
